pr_title: SSKDF with KMAC should return SIZE_MAX when EVP_KDF_CTX_get_kdf_size() is used
pr_body:
Fixes #19934

The existing code was looking for the digest size, and then returned zero.

The example code in EVP_KDF-SS.pod has been corrected to not use a digest for KMAC

issue_context.title: SSKDF with KMAC: "missing message digest"
issue_context.body:
OpenSSL version: 3.0.7

When trying to derive keys using SSKDF with KMAC128 or KMAC256, OpenSSL returns an error:
```
40671FF4307F0000:error:1C800081:Provider routines:sskdf_size:missing message digest:providers/implementations/kdfs/sskdf.c:338:
```

However, the [man page](https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.0/man7/EVP_KDF-SS.html) mentions that the digest parameter is only required for hash-based and HMAC-based SSKDF. Why does the SSKDF implementation assume the digest is present: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.0/providers/implementations/kdfs/sskdf.c#L332-L343?

Perhaps the `ctx->out_len` value should be checked here first? This value is set by `OSSL_KDF_PARAM_MAC_SIZE` here: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.0/providers/implementations/kdfs/sskdf.c#L475-L480
comments:
Also note that the man page example for KMAC128 also sets the digest parameter to SHA-256, for some reason?
```
*p++ = OSSL_PARAM_construct_utf8_string(OSSL_KDF_PARAM_DIGEST,
                                        SN_sha256, strlen(SN_sha256));
```

The pod example seems wrong..

There is an example of how to set up a kmac in evp_kdf_ss_kmac (see test_kdf_ss_kmac).
It does not need the digest. (KMAC uses CSHAKE (SHAKE internally)).
Can you provide the code you are using please, so I can see the difference between this and the expected usage in the test.?
The output length is whatever size you want?
i.e One of the inputs to KMAC is the output length - since it is variable size..

According to https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.0/man3/EVP_KDF_CTX_get_kdf_size.html:
> EVP_KDF_CTX_get_kdf_size() returns the output size if the algorithm produces a fixed amount of output and SIZE_MAX otherwise. If an error occurs then 0 is returned. For some algorithms an error may result if input parameters necessary to calculate a fixed output size have not yet been supplied.

So perhaps the KMAC length isn't the right output, but it should be SIZE_MAX?

Yeah probably, but I would tend to think that in the example that you present that you wouldnt want to call it at all? What use is a return value of SIZE_MAX to you use case?. I can change the code, but it doesnt really help you.
You may want to free the kdf, ctx, params and bld..

Fair enough.. You could potentially have truncated values for the else case that are valid so that logic might not be quite right..
I better go and check the code I added for KBKDF to support KMAC a few days ago - it may have the same size related problem.. Thanks.

> You could potentially have truncated values for the else case that are valid so that logic might not be quite right..

What do you mean?
I mean the output length can be less than the digest size.
See the test vectors in test/recipies/30_test_evp_data/evpkdf_ss.txt for SHA1
Thanks, that makes sense, I'll fix that

review_comments: Maybe use some bogus digest name?

What I was trying to do here is just test that it doesnt fail and it gets the correct output. I dont think it should care what it does with the digest (whether the implementation 'completely' ignores it or not does not really matter).
I'd just skip this with ctx->is_kmac
I dont think this matters much. I took ignored to mean not used for the algorithm.
This is also affected by the order params are loaded in. So ctx->is_kmac could be true after setting the digest.
